question: Should OpenClaw expose a configurable exec approval timeout, and if so what public key, precedence, maximum, and fail-closed semantics should it use?
rationale: This changes public config/env surface for a host-exec authorization window, so code inspection can prove the gap but cannot choose the security/product contract safely.

options.title: Define a bounded timeout contract
options.body: Add one maintainer-approved key with a conservative maximum and thread it through every approval registration and wait path with docs and focused tests.

options.title: Keep the fixed default
options.body: Leave the 30-minute default as the only supported behavior and close duplicate configurability requests as not planned.

options.title: Solve via operator UX only
options.body: Improve notices, Control UI recovery, or setup hints without adding a new timeout configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Define a bounded timeout contract
recommendation.body: Add one maintainer-approved key with a conservative maximum and thread it through every approval registration and wait path with docs and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing history and prior review comments route the timeout/config decision through this exec approval surface.
